reden: Yes. The audit explicitly reports that Float128.sqrt() uses the EVM STOP opcode when input is zero, halting the entire call frame instead of returning 0. This is the same issue as the described vulnerability: same function and code path (zero-input branch of sqrt), same mechanism (STOP-caused silent termination), same impact (subsequent logic skipped/odd caller behavior), and the same fix (return 0 instead of STOP). Fixing the audit’s issue would fix the described vulnerability.
